correctness.rationale: Standard finite bounded commutative BCK decomposition reduces to the equispaced rational grids. An equation counterexample on a grid of denominator n0-1 differs by at least its reciprocal; the difference of terms has Lipschitz constant at most the number L of variable occurrences. A violating box of side 1/[4L(n0-1)] yields a violating fraction >=[16L(n0-1)]^-k on all sufficiently fine grids. On coarser grids, any violation gives >= n^-k, bounded below by the same threshold. Multiplication of satisfaction degrees over chain products completes the argument. The included exact-rational verifier returns VERIFY_OK on n=2..50 for one nontrivial law.

value.rationale: The quantitative uniform gap directly addresses Evans’s stated classification question for bounded commutative BCK equations, showing that every equation in any fixed arity either holds identically or admits a strict uniform finite-algebra separation. A witness-level syntactic formula gives an effective nonzero bound. This is a class-wide logical principle, not a named-identity special-case recomputation.
